uncited: PixelSplat Training and Depth Regularization is a two-phase optimization procedure for generalizable 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) that combines standard photometric reconstruction with geometric consistency priors.

It solves the problem of producing high-quality point clouds from sparse or monocular inputs by first learning to render accurate RGB images and then refining the depth estimates via a regularization loss.

It differs from its siblings by explicitly placing multiple Gaussians per ray to enable multi-depth gradients and using a discrete depth regularization term based on second-order derivatives, whereas [SparseGS](6135-sparsegs.md) and [DNGaussian](7399-dngaussian.md) rely on different sparse or implicit priors, and [Edge-Aware Disparity Regularization](9140-edge-aware-disparity-regularization.md) focuses on disparity space smoothing.
- A batch of scenes, each with $N$ reference views (RGB images).
- (Optional) Ground truth depth maps for the depth regularization phase.
- A set of 3D Gaussians (position, covariance, color, opacity) for each scene.
- Rendered RGB images and depth maps for target views.

- **Gaussian:** Defined by mean position $\mu \in \mathbb{R}^3$, covariance matrix $\Sigma \in \mathbb{R}^{3 \times 3}$ (or rotation/scale parameters), color $c \in \mathbb{R}^3$, and opacity $\alpha \in [0, 1]$.
- **Ray Probability Distribution:** A distribution $P(z)$ along the viewing ray, from which Gaussian centers are sampled.
For each pixel in the target view, cast a ray.
Compute the depth regularization loss $L_{reg\_depth}$ based on these differences.
SparSplat Training Objective is a variant that uses end-to-end training with multi-view RGB and ground truth depth supervision, freezing deep feature networks for efficiency.
It builds on 3D Gaussian Splatting [19] and generalizable reconstruction techniques.
The depth regularization technique is designed to enhance the geometric quality of the reconstructed point clouds.
